item.title: [SwiftHFR] Posting: fetch the form at send with legacy's 60 s idle limit (#1375)
item.body:
## Issue
Refs #1375. Left on the issue: the list-load timeouts, which wait for the device trace (diagnosis: https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/1375#issuecomment-7214723426).
Claim: cloud/i1375-opus
Author model: Opus 5.5 (cloud/i1375-opus)
Reviewer model: Fable 5.2 (cloud/i1375-fable-r1, cloud/i1375-fable-r2)

## What and why
- **Problem**: sending from the composer failed with « Le forum ne répond pas : rien n'a été envoyé » (operator screenshot, #1375), while legacy posted on the same network at the same moment.
- **Cause**: that message is `ComposerMessages.network(.timedOut)`, the « nothing was sent » branch. It comes from the **form fetch** that runs before the POST; a POST timeout would show « n'a pas confirmé l'envoi » instead. `PostingFlow.loadForm` fetched the form with the list loads' 10 s idle limit. Legacy fetched the same forms with a plain `URLRequest(url:)`, so it got URLSession's 60 s idle default (all @ `87fe0d1c`):
  - reply form: `HFRswift/Swift/ReplyService.swift:238-243`
  - quote form, and the edit form through `fetchQuoteTemplate` (`MessagesView.swift:4325-4334`): `:804-809`
  - delete form: `:1046-1047`
  - moderator-alert form: `:1463-1470`
- **Change**:
  - `PostingFlow.formTimeout = 60`. `loadForm` uses it by default, so every form fetched for a write gets it: reply, new topic, MP, edit, delete, quote, prefill and options reads, plus the moderator-alert form (`ModeratorAlertFlow.prepare`).
  - Background reads keep 10 s by passing `timeout:`: the MPStorage forms (legacy went through ASI's 10 s, `Classes/MPStorage.m:769-775`) and the group-roster re-read after a confirmed change.
  - Unchanged: the POST was already 60 s, and the list, topic-page and search limits stay at legacy's 10 s.
  - Docs: `HFR-PROTOCOL.md` (timeouts line) and LOT-048 step 1 give the limits.

## How it was verified
- New or extended tests, each pinning one limit:
  - `PostingCaptureTests.formFetchUsesLegacyLimit`: form GET = 60, no total cap.
  - `QuoteCaptureTests.singleQuote`: quote GET = 60.
  - `ModeratorAlertSubmitTests`: alert form GET = 60.
  - `MPStorageTransportWriteTests`: both storage GETs = 10.
  - `GroupRosterTests`: form, POST, re-read = `[60, 60, 10]`.
- Each assertion was shown red without its source change. The reviewer re-ran the mutations independently.
- Full `swift test` on Linux: 2213 tests in 257 suites passed.
- Fable adversarial review: REQUEST CHANGES in round 1 (3 findings, all fixed in `3a35e26`), then APPROVE in round 2. Both verdicts are posted on this PR.

## Checklist (AGENTS.md §9)
- [x] Module boundaries respected (only `HFRClient`)
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] No secrets; fixtures anonymized (existing captures only)
- [x] Docs updated (`HFR-PROTOCOL.md`, LOT-048)
- [x] Author model: Opus 5.5 / Reviewer model: Fable 5.2
- [x] No legacy-app behaviour change, no gap row: no `### Ledger`

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (Fable 5.2, cloud/i1375-fable-r1, round 1): REQUEST CHANGES** — head 588338a

1. **Medium — `Packages/HFRKit/Sources/HFRClient/Alert/ModeratorAlertFlow.swift:92`** (not in the diff). The alert form GET stays at 10 s on the PR body's citation of `AlerteModoViewController.m:38`. That is the Obj-C reader's path. The SwiftUI reader this PR cites for quote, edit and delete calls `ForumModerationAlertService.prepareAlert` (`MessagesView.swift:4595` → `ReplyService.swift:1463-1470` @ 87fe0d1c), a plain `URLRequest`, so 60 s. LOT-004 names that service the live side, and our alert POST already uses `postTimeout`. Scenario: forum silent 10-60 s before the first byte, legacy opens the alert form, SwiftHFR fails. Fix: give `prepare` `PostingFlow.formTimeout` with a test, or justify 10 s with both legacy paths cited.

2. **Low — `PostingFlow.swift:133`**. `loadForm` also serves callers the PR body does not list: `MPStorageTransport.swift:185,203` and `GroupRosterFlow.swift:102`. Legacy MPStorage requests were ASI at 10 s (`Classes/MPStorage.m:772-775`, `ASIHTTPRequest.m:53`). Scenario: a silent forum now holds an MPStorage sync, and the optional roster re-read after a confirmed change, up to 60 s instead of 10. Fix: a `timeout` parameter on the internal `loadForm`, keeping `RequestTimeout.standard` for those callers, or a recorded decision in the specs.

3. **Detail — `docs/lots/LOT-048-post-form-engine.md:32`**. Step 1 (Load) does not state the 60 s limit; step 7 states the POST's. `HFR-PROTOCOL.md` should also state the alert form's limit once finding 1 is settled.

**Verified**
- The four `ReplyService.swift` ranges (183, 238-243, 804-809, 1046-1047) and `MessagesView.swift:4325-4334` match 87fe0d1c; these services build `URLSessionConfiguration.default` with no timeout set, so 60 s idle.
- Mutation: with the `timeout:` argument removed, `PostingCaptureTests` and `QuoteCaptureTests` fail (5 issues, `10.0 == 60`); green on head. 250 tests of the Posting, Quote, roster, MPStorage and alert suites pass.
- No app-side wrapper shortens the call (`ReplyPosting.swift:165-210`); the transport passes `timeout` to `timeoutInterval`.
- Changed Swift lines are ≤ 140 columns. SwiftLint and the full suite were not run.
- Poll vote, MP delete and flag POSTs keep 10 s; not compared with legacy here.

**Round 1 fixes** in `3a35e26`, one commit:
1. ✅ The moderator alert form is now 60 s (`ModeratorAlertFlow.prepare`: `.get(link, timeout: PostingFlow.formTimeout)`). The legacy SwiftUI reader's `prepareAlert` used a plain `URLRequest` (`ReplyService.swift:1463-1470` @ `87fe0d1c`). Pinned in `ModeratorAlertSubmitTests` (form GET `timeout == 60`).
2. ✅ The internal `loadForm` takes a `timeout`, 60 s by default. MPStorage keeps 10 s (`MPStorageTransport.formTimeout = RequestTimeout.standard`, legacy ASI `Classes/MPStorage.m:769-775`, `ASIHTTPRequest.m:53`), and so does the group-roster re-read. Pinned in `MPStorageTransportWriteTests` (both storage GETs at 10) and `GroupRosterTests` (`[60, 60, 10]`: form, POST, re-read).
3. ✅ LOT-048 step 1 and `HFR-PROTOCOL.md` now give the limits, including the alert form and the MPStorage and roster exceptions.

Mutation check: with the round-1 source changes reverted, all 4 new assertions fail (`60 == 10` ×3, alert `10 == 60`). Full `swift test` on Linux: 2213 tests passed.

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (Fable 5.2, cloud/i1375-fable-r2, round 2): APPROVE** — head 3a35e26

No open finding. Round-1 findings:

1. **Fixed (was Medium)** — `Packages/HFRKit/Sources/HFRClient/Alert/ModeratorAlertFlow.swift:93`: the alert form GET now uses `PostingFlow.formTimeout`, citing `ReplyService.swift:1463-1470` @ 87fe0d1c (`prepareAlert`, plain `URLRequest`; citation checked). `ModeratorAlertSubmitTests.swift:37` asserts it.

2. **Fixed (was Low)** — `PostingFlow.loadForm` takes a `timeout` (default `formTimeout`). `MPStorageTransport.swift:189-191,209` pass `RequestTimeout.standard` through `MPStorageTransport.formTimeout`, and `GroupRosterFlow.swift:103` passes it for the re-read. `Classes/MPStorage.m:769-775` (`GETRequest`, ASI, no timeout set) and `ASIHTTPRequest.m:53` (default 10) match 87fe0d1c. The roster write's own form fetch keeps 60 s, as a composer form.

3. **Fixed (was Detail)** — `docs/lots/LOT-048-post-form-engine.md:34` states the 60 s load; the `HFR-PROTOCOL.md` timeouts line covers the alert form and the 10 s exceptions.

**Verified**
- Mutation on 3a35e26: with the alert GET, the MPStorage constant and the roster re-read each reverted, `ModeratorAlertSubmitTests`, `MPStorageTransportWriteTests` (two tests) and `GroupRosterTests` fail (4 issues); the round-1 mutation of `loadForm` had failed `PostingCaptureTests` and `QuoteCaptureTests`.
- On head, 250 tests of the Posting, Quote, roster, MPStorage and alert suites pass; SwiftLint is silent on the changed Swift files; no changed Swift line exceeds 140 columns.
- Every `loadForm` caller: app composer calls (`App/SwiftHFR/Composer/ReplyPosting.swift:165-210`) and `QuoteFlow.swift:94` get 60 s; MPStorage and the roster re-read get 10 s.
- Not run: the full suite and the app build (Linux session). Poll vote, MP delete and flag POSTs keep 10 s and were not compared with legacy; they are outside this PR.
